answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks using clock-skew fingerprinting tied to physical variations in each node's quartz oscillator. Peers measure timestamp drift during routine challenges, mapping valid skew profiles into a decentralized atlas. An attacker incurs the direct hardware cost of purchasing dedicated physical oscillators per identity, rendering hollow virtual clones detectable. However, ambient temperature shifts alter drift rates, risking false rejections of honest nodes.
